[1/4] Plan declarative material graphs: frozen node graph with color/float/checker/texture/mix/material nodes, topological evaluation with cycle detection, JSON serialization, registry texture resolution, tests, docs and ADR-028

impact_assessment.why: Materials are literal Material values, so reusable procedural surfaces, texture references and mixes must be rebuilt by hand in every game and cannot be serialized, inspected or compared by AI clients.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients get an immutable, deterministic, JSON-serializable material graph that evaluates to one Material, resolves textures by name or AssetRegistry id, and needs no OpenGL or new dependency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.material_graph module plus MaterialGraph/MaterialGraphNode exports and version 0.23.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus the existing geometry, math3d and texture modules only; concurrency: pure evaluation with no shared state or background work; state: no persisted files, graphs are in-memory documents
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for constant color/float, checker textures, mix, cycle and bad-graph validation, deterministic evaluation, JSON round trips, texture-by-name resolution and registry resolution; full 6/6 project gate before delivery

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Material graph core and serialization: MaterialGraphNode/MaterialGraph with normalized frozen params and inputs, topological evaluation with cycle detection, color/float/checker/texture/mix/material nodes, JSON to_dict/from_dict, registry texture resolution; 7 new tests, ruff clean, 6/6 gates; checklists: passed

[1/4] Plan dependency-free glTF 2.0 import: package with io, textures, materials, meshes, scene and loader modules; buffers, accessors, meshes, PBR materials, PNG textures, node/scene hierarchy, TRS and matrix transforms; tests, docs and ADR-029

impact_assessment.why: Keystone could load OBJ and PNG assets but had no path for modern glTF scenes, forcing asset conversion or hand-built meshes.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients can import glTF 2.0 scenes, meshes, materials and textures without new dependencies or OpenGL, with optional AssetRegistry registration.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.gltf package plus GltfImport/load_gltf exports and version 0.24.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus existing geometry, math3d, scene and texture modules only; concurrency: pure import with no shared state; state: no persisted files, inputs are read-only
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for triangle meshes, materials, translation, files, version validation, missing positions, embedded PNG textures, external buffers and registry registration; full 6/6 project gate before delivery

checkpoints.description: [2/4] glTF import core: package with io, textures, materials, meshes, scene and loader; typed accessor decoding, PNG textures, PBR material conversion, mesh decoding with normals/UVs/colors/indices, node and scene construction with TRS and matrix transforms; 8 tests, ruff clean, 6/6 gates; checklists: passed

[1/4] Plan versioned scene snapshots and undo/redo history: History stack, scene_to_dict/scene_from_dict with asset references, tests, docs and ADR-030

impact_assessment.why: The engine had no way to save, restore or roll back a scene graph without OpenGL or a game-specific serializer.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients can save, restore and roll back scene graphs without OpenGL, with asset references and bounded undo/redo.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.history and keystone.scene_snapshot modules plus exports and version 0.25.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus existing scene, math3d and assets modules only; concurrency: pure in-memory state with no shared locks; state: snapshots are in memory, mesh and material payloads are referenced by asset id
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for undo/redo, capacity, deep copy, version validation, round trips and asset reattachment; full 6/6 project gate before delivery

checkpoints.description: [2/4] History and scene snapshots: History deep-copies snapshots and bounds capacity; scene_to_dict/scene_from_dict version 1 preserve identity, hierarchy, tags, layer, visibility, transforms, camera and asset references; 11 tests, ruff clean, 6/6 gates; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-state-history-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan a correctness pass over the recent glTF, material-graph and scene-snapshot work: fix indexed normal generation, primitive-mode validation, node-cycle detection, normalized/sparse accessor handling, snapshot environment fidelity and malformed-document validation; sync docs and roadmap; ship with tests and gates

impact_assessment.why: The recent v0.23-v0.25 features were delivered without a focused adversarial review, and inspection found real correctness gaps: glTF normals are generated from vertex order rather than triangle indices, non-triangle primitives are misread as triangles, cyclic node graphs recurse instead of failing cleanly, normalized integer accessors yield unnormalized colors, sparse accessors silently decode as zeros, and scene snapshots drop environment/lighting state while accepting duplicate ids and dangling parents.
impact_assessment.benefits: Imported meshes shade correctly and malformed files fail with clear validation errors instead of wrong geometry, recursion or silent zeros; saved scenes restore their full visual environment and reject corrupt hierarchies; documentation stops claiming shipped features are future work.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: same public modules and schema versions, stricter validation may reject documents that previously loaded silently; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none, all pure decoding; state: scene snapshot documents gain optional camera and environment fields while staying schema 1 and backwards compatible
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for each bug, full pytest suite plus the project 6/6 Phase 4 gate, ruff and secret scan before commit

checkpoints.description: [2/3] glTF and snapshot correctness: normals now follow triangle indices; non-triangle modes, unknown material indices, sparse accessors and node cycles fail with ValueError; normalized integer accessors scale to unit range; snapshots preserve camera lens, ambient/background/sky, fog and lights and reject duplicate ids, dangling parents and self-parenting; material texture_name must resolve; 7 glTF, 6 snapshot and 1 material-graph regression tests added

[1/3] Plan a second format pass over the last three commits: add GLB container import, validate glTF material texture indices and accessor view bounds, enforce snapshot asset kinds and field types, and remove the quadratic asset lookup; tests, ADR, docs and version bump

impact_assessment.why: The recent glTF and snapshot hardening still leaves real gaps: binary .glb files are rejected as invalid UTF-8 JSON, material baseColorTexture indices are silently dropped when out of range, accessor byte offsets can read outside their declared bufferView, and scene snapshots accept a material asset as a node mesh and coerce non-string ids. These failures are silent or surface as confusing downstream errors.
impact_assessment.benefits: Keystone imports standard GLB bundles and fails malformed glTF and snapshot documents early with precise errors; asset references are type-checked, and snapshot serialization scales linearly instead of scanning the whole registry per node.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: same public modules, GLB added to load_gltf input and version 0.26.0; stricter validation may reject previously accepted malformed documents; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none, pure decoding; state: no persisted format change beyond accepting GLB input
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for GLB JSON and BIN chunks, texture index validation, accessor bounds, snapshot kind mismatch and non-string ids; full pytest, ruff and 6/6 project gates before commit

checkpoints.description: [2/3] GLB and validation: load_gltf accepts GLB v2 JSON and BIN chunks from bytes or files; material texture indices, accessor/bufferView offsets and view bounds are validated; snapshots require string ids, reject non-mapping camera/transform, enforce mesh/material asset kinds and use a linear payload-to-id index; 8 glTF and 3 snapshot regressions added
